answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging for identity with verifiable work tied to time: each new agent must complete a costly, unique task, like carving a marble tile by hand, before its votes count. Weight then grows only through sustained honest output, not account count. A swarm of fakes stalls on that ledge, since mixing a thousand identities is like diluting one pigment into a thousand pots: each copy carries too little color to sway consensus.
